patient.name: Robert Kimura
patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral foot tingling and numbness for 2 years in a patient with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma
patient.hpi: Robert Kimura is a 53-year-old retired financial analyst who was diagnosed with IgG kappa multiple myeloma 6 months ago and has been receiving bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (VRd) chemotherapy. He now presents to neurology for evaluation of bilateral foot tingling and numbness that began 6 weeks after his first bortezomib cycle and has progressively worsened over 4 cycles. The symptoms began in the bilateral great toes and have spread to involve all toes and the forefoot on both sides. He describes the sensation as 'electric shocks with pins and needles' predominantly, with a burning component at night. He also notes bilateral fingertip tingling that began 2 weeks ago. He does not have significant weakness, though he notices mild clumsiness with buttons. He denies ataxia or falls. His oncologist has been monitoring him and has already dose-reduced bortezomib from 1.3 mg/m² to 1.0 mg/m² after cycle 3 due to these symptoms. He has no prior history of neuropathy, no diabetes, no alcohol use. He was an active runner prior to his myeloma diagnosis and is very motivated to return to running if possible.

report.summary: MILDLY ABNORMAL NCS/EMG. LENGTH-DEPENDENT SENSORY AXONAL NEUROPATHY — consistent with bortezomib-induced neuropathy (predominantly sensory, DRG-mediated). Mild reduction in sural SNAP amplitude bilaterally with preserved motor NCS. Early course of drug-induced neuropathy.

emg.summary: Normal EMG — no denervation. Consistent with early/mild axonal sensory neuropathy without significant axonal loss yet.

report.overall_impression: Mild sensory-predominant axonal neuropathy. Sural SNAP amplitudes mildly reduced bilaterally. Superficial peroneal SNAP low-normal. Motor NCS within normal limits. Needle EMG shows no spontaneous activity and normal motor unit recruitment. Findings are consistent with a mild length-dependent sensory axonal neuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

Findings are consistent with a mild length-dependent sensory axonal neuropathy with predominant distal lower extremity sensory involvement and no motor axon loss at this time

output.query: bortezomib peripheral neuropathy management dose modification IMWG

results.citation: Moreau P et al. (2011) Subcutaneous versus intravenous bortezomib for myeloma. Lancet Oncol 12:431-440.
results.summary: Subcutaneous bortezomib (SC) reduces grade ≥3 PN from 16% (IV) to 6% with equivalent efficacy. SC dosing is now standard of care. Grade 1: 1.3 mg/m² dose maintained. Grade 2: dose reduce to 1.0 mg/m². Grade 3: hold bortezomib, resume at 0.7 mg/m² when ≤grade 1. Grade 4: discontinue permanently.

results.citation: Richardson PG et al. (2012) Prevention and management of treatment-emergent peripheral neuropathy in multiple myeloma. J Clin Oncol 30:3573-3580.
results.summary: Weekly bortezomib administration (rather than twice-weekly) reduces neuropathy incidence. SC route preferred. Symptoms often partially reversible after discontinuation. Carfilzomib or ixazomib are alternatives with lower neurotoxicity for patients with significant BiPN.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Bortezomib-induced peripheral neuropathy (CTCAE grade 2) in multiple myeloma

differential.key_features: Anti-MAG / amyloid / CIDP-like patterns can occur; need SPEP/IFE and consider nerve biopsy if persistent.

differential.diagnosis: Spinal cord / nerve root compression from myeloma deposits
differential.key_features: Plain X-ray, MRI spine; lytic lesions, vertebral collapse.
No diabetes here; sometimes coexisting risk factor.
Painful small-fiber + autonomic + cardiac amyloidosis; fat-pad / nerve biopsy with Congo red.
Predominantly axonal pattern argues against; would need demyelinating NCS + CSF.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains and bone marrow re-evaluation (rule out paraprotein-driven neuropathy and disease progression)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Stable IgG kappa monoclonal protein per known myeloma; absence of new IgM or increasing M-spike

optimal_actions.action: Skin biopsy for intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IENFD below 97.5% lower limit for age/sex confirms small-fiber neuropathy

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize bortezomib as a known cause of painful axonal sensory + small-fiber neuropathy
Dose-modify, switch to subcutaneous, or transition to alternative agent (carfilzomib, daratumumab-based regimen)
Re-evaluate myeloma status (SPEP/IFE/light chains) to rule out paraprotein-driven neuropathy or progression
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue full-dose IV bortezomib in symptomatic CTCAE ≥grade 2 neuropathy without dose modification
Do not attribute to diabetes when patient has no diabetes
key_reasoning_points: Painful predominantly sensory axonal neuropathy in a myeloma patient on bortezomib has a high pre-test probability of drug toxicity
Switch to subcutaneous / dose reduction or alternative regimen typically improves symptoms
Still confirm no paraprotein-driven (anti-MAG / amyloid) component
